page.h1: HTS Chapter 70: Glass and Glassware — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariff on U.S. Glass by Country: Canada, China, EU, Mexico (HTS Ch. 70) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Canada, the EU, Mexico, Japan, China, Korea, the UK and India charge on U.S. fiberglass, mirrors, bottles, flat glass and glassware, market by market.

intro: Most U.S. glass enters its big markets duty-free. **Canada, Mexico and Korea** charge 0% on goods that qualify for their trade agreements, the **EU** has charged 0% on U.S.-origin glass since July 1, 2026 (normally up to 11%), and **Japan** charges 0% on mirrors, fiberglass and most other lines. Two exceptions cost money: **Canada's 50% surtax** on U.S. glass bottles and jars (7010.90) since September 8, 2026, and **China**, where U.S. glass pays its normal 7–15% rate plus a 10–25% counter-tariff plus a 10% extra duty, 27–50% in all unless the importer holds an exclusion. **India** charges 10–20% and the **UK** 6–7% on fiberglass and 10% on glassware. Where the tariff is zero, the buyer's product rules decide access instead: vehicle type approval for rear-view mirrors and safety glass, food-contact rules for bottles and tableware.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada is the largest market ($1.71B, up 0.7%): fiberglass (7019, $402M), float glass (7005, $286M), glass bottles and jars (7010, $259M), car mirrors (7009, $259M) and safety glass and insulating units for its window and vehicle plants. Everything enters free under CUSMA except glass containers, which have paid a 50% surtax since September 8, 2026, even when they qualify. Bottles used to package food or drinks, or used in manufacturing, can get the surtax back.

profile.headline: The EU ($1.08B, down 2.5%) buys mostly vehicle rear-view mirrors (7009, $525M, almost all to Germany), then fiberglass (7019, $158M), laboratory glassware (7017, $90M) and signalling glass (7014, $74M). Since July 1, 2026 every U.S. glass line enters at 0%, against 4% on mirrors, 7% on fiberglass and 11% on glassware before. The EU's countermeasure list of 2025, which had much of the chapter at 25–30%, stays suspended.
profile.mainProducts: Mirrors, incl. vehicle rear-view mirrors (7009) · Glass fibers: fiberglass yarn, rovings, mats, fabric & glass wool (7019)

regulator.name: EU vehicle type approval (Regulation (EU) 2019/2144) and food-contact rules (Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004)
regulator.requirement: Rear-view mirrors and safety glazing for cars and trucks must be type-approved to UN Regulations No 46 and No 43, which Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 requires. Glass bottles, jars and tableware that touch food must meet the general safety rules of Regulation (EC) No 1935/2004

profile.headline: Mexico ($885M, down 17.4%) is the largest buyer of U.S. fiberglass (7019, $466M) for its composite, auto-parts and appliance plants, followed by car mirrors (7009, $152M) and safety glass (7007, $69M). assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in November 2026. They come from the WITS (TRAINS) simple-average MFN applied rate for one representative six-digit subheading per heading, the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 7009.10 for rear-view mirrors, 7019.90 for glass fibres, 7010.90 for bottles and jars, 7005.10 for float glass and 7017.90 for laboratory glassware), for 2023, the latest year WITS holds. They are updated where a national 2026 schedule or notice was checked: EU TARIC, the UK Trade Tariff, Mexico's December 2025 decree, China's 2026 provisional rates and Canada's surtax orders. National 8–10-digit lines can differ.

Canada, Mexico and Korea show the free-trade-agreement rate for goods that qualify; the normal-rate column shows the MFN rate a non-qualifying good pays. Mexico's normal rates include the increases of January 1, 2026.

Canada's 7010 cells add the 50% surtax of the United States Surtax Order (2026) on tariff item 7010.90.00. Remission for containers used to package food or beverages, or in manufacturing, is on Export rules.
The EU cells show 0% for U.S.-origin goods under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 from July 1, 2026; the normal-rate column shows the third-country duty other origins pay.

China's cells add three layers: China's 2026 rate (provisional where one exists, otherwise MFN), the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, and the 2018–2019 counter-tariff of the line (10%, 20% or 25%). An importer with an exclusion pays only the first two.
India's cells show basic customs duty only.
Trade agreements that are signed or announced but not in force (Taiwan, Malaysia, Thailand, India) are not applied; see Tariff updates.
